topics_checked.note: EU registration certificate (optional, portal.gov.cz); non-EU long-term visa and long-term residence permit for study (ipc.gov.cz, Ministry of the Interior).
Reporting place of residence: EU within 30 days, non-EU within 3 working days (ipc.gov.cz).
No separate tax-ID application for students: the Ministry of the Interior assigns a personal identity number (rodne cislo) ex officio. Tax residency rule for students from Financni sprava.
EHIC use (European Commission, Charles University), non-EU comprehensive insurance (ipc.gov.cz, CU), public insurance via employment (VZP).
Only the EU-wide basic payment account right (Your Europe) and the CU rule that bursaries are paid only to Czech accounts were found; no Czech authority page on documents banks require.
PID (Prague) student season tickets under 26; CU student card works as PID pass (pid.cz, cuni.cz). Prices in subsidies.json and cities/prague.json.
Free access to the labour market (ipc.gov.cz), CU Work and Study page, DPP agreement 300 h/year (MPSV) and DPP insurance threshold (VZP).
MPSV press releases for 2026 and 2027 amounts. No youth or student sub-minimum found on these pages.

items.title: EU/EEA/Swiss citizens: no permit needed; optional temporary residence certificate
items.title_it: Cittadini UE/SEE/svizzeri: nessun permesso; certificato di soggiorno temporaneo facoltativo
items.summary: EU citizens can stay and study without a permit. For stays over 3 months they may apply for a registration certificate (temporary residence certificate), but it is not a requirement for the stay. Applications go to a Ministry of the Interior (OAMP/DAMP) office, by post or electronically; documents include travel document, proof of study purpose, photo, health insurance and proof of accommodation.
steps: Collect travel document/ID, enrolment confirmation, 1 photo, proof of health insurance, proof of accommodation (non-original documents no older than 180 days)
Apply in person at the Ministry of the Interior office for your district, by post, or via data box/e-mail with electronic signature
items.authority: Ministry of the Interior (Department for Asylum and Migration Policy)
items.notes: The page lists Swiss and EEA citizens implicitly under 'EU citizen' rules via ipc.gov.cz (EU plus Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, Switzerland). Processing time not stated.

items.title: Non-EU students: long-term visa for study (up to 1 year)
items.title_it: Studenti extra-UE: visto di lungo periodo per studio (fino a 1 anno)

applies_to.stay_duration: more than 90 days, maximum 1 year in total

items.summary: Third-country nationals studying under Section 64 of the Residence Act (accredited university programmes, preparatory courses, exchange programmes) get a long-term visa for study, valid at most 1 year. Apply in person at a Czech embassy (with appointment). Required: application form, passport, proof of accommodation, proof of funds, photo, enrolment confirmation, criminal record extract, and travel medical insurance.
steps: Book an appointment at the competent Czech embassy
Submit form, passport, accommodation, funds, photo, original enrolment confirmation, criminal record extract
Before the visa is placed: show insurance (emergency care first 90 days + comprehensive for the rest, or comprehensive for the whole stay)
items.cost: CZK 2,500 consular fee; extension fee CZK 1,000 does not apply to students (ipc.gov.cz, 2026-11-25)
items.authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs (embassies) / Ministry of the Interior

items.title: Non-EU students: long-term residence permit for study (stays over 1 year)
items.title_it: Studenti extra-UE: permesso di soggiorno di lungo periodo per studio (oltre 1 anno)
items.summary: For stays longer than one year (e.g. full degrees) a long-term residence permit for study is needed. It is valid up to 1 year (2 years in cases set by law) and renewable. It can be requested at an embassy or, if already in Czechia on a qualifying visa/permit, in person at a Ministry of the Interior office. Comprehensive medical insurance and proof of funds are required.
items.notes: Students already holding an EU study permit from another member state (except Ireland, Denmark) may study in Czechia up to 1 year without a visa if 'student' is on the card (ipc.gov.cz).

items.title: Non-EU students: proof of funds for a study visa/permit
items.title_it: Studenti extra-UE: prova dei mezzi economici per visto/permesso di studio
items.summary: Funds required = 15 x the subsistence minimum plus 2 x the subsistence minimum for each further whole month. The Ministry page uses CZK 3,130 as subsistence minimum, giving CZK 78,250 for one semester (Sep-Feb) and CZK 115,810 for a full year (Sep-Aug). Under-18s prove half. A school or public body covering all costs, or a grant under an international agreement, can replace it.
items.notes: The page says the CZK 3,130 amount applies 'since 1 January 2023'. CZK 3,130 equals MPSV's existence minimum (existencni minimum), still CZK 3,130 on the MPSV page updated 1 Oct 2026; MPSV's separate living minimum for an individual rose to CZK 5,500. Confirm with the embassy if in doubt.

interpretations.hypothesis: The 'subsistence minimum' used is the existence minimum, unchanged at CZK 3,130/month, so the totals (CZK 78,250 per semester, CZK 115,810 per year) still apply.
If the authority instead referred to the living minimum (CZK 5,500 for an individual from 1 Oct 2026), the required totals would be higher; the ministry page does not say so.

items.title: EU citizens: report your place of residence within 30 days
items.title_it: Cittadini UE: dichiarare il luogo di residenza entro 30 giorni
items.summary: If you plan to stay more than 30 days you must report your place of residence to the Foreign Police within 30 days of entry, unless your accommodation provider (hotel, hostel, dormitory) reports you or you are under 15. Later address changes must be reported within 30 working days if you will live at the new address more than 180 days.
items.authority: Foreign Police / Ministry of the Interior

items.title: Non-EU students: register within 3 working days (30 days with a D/VR visa)
items.title_it: Studenti extra-UE: registrazione entro 3 giorni lavorativi (30 giorni con visto D/VR)
items.summary: Third-country nationals must report their place of residence within 3 working days of arrival (Foreign Police for long-term visa holders), unless the dormitory/hotel registers them. Holders of a D/VR visa (issued to collect a residence permit) must register at a Ministry of the Interior office within 30 calendar days, where biometrics are also taken.
items.deadline: 3 working days; 30 calendar days with D/VR visa
items.authority: Foreign Police / Ministry of the Interior

items.title: Personal identity number (rodne cislo) is assigned automatically
items.title_it: Il numero personale (rodne cislo) viene assegnato d'ufficio
items.summary: Foreigners staying temporarily or permanently receive a personal identity number (rodne cislo) from the Ministry of the Interior ex officio, usually requested at the first visit (registration or registration-certificate application). It appears on the registration certificate or residence permit card; a long-term visa does not show it. Schools, banks, insurers and doctors may ask for it.
items.notes: The Ministry does not notify you when the number is assigned; ask in person at a Ministry office. The page does not describe a separate tax ID (DIC) procedure for employees.

items.title: Staying in Czechia only to study makes you a tax non-resident
items.title_it: Chi soggiorna in Cechia solo per studio e' non residente fiscale
items.summary: The Financial Administration states that a person staying in Czechia only for study or medical treatment is a tax non-resident, even if they habitually stay there. Non-residents are taxed only on Czech-source income. Most employees do not need to file a return because the employer settles tax monthly (Charles University).

items.title: EU/EEA/Swiss students: EHIC, register it with a Czech insurer
items.title_it: Studenti UE/SEE/svizzeri: TEAM (EHIC), da registrare presso un assicuratore ceco
items.summary: The EHIC covers necessary care only at doctors contracted with a Czech public insurer; you pay only standard patient fees (CZK 90 for emergency services). For longer stays you can register the EHIC with a Czech insurer and get a registration certificate; Charles University tells EU/EFTA students to register after arrival. Mountain rescue and repatriation are not covered.
items.authority: Czech public health insurers / European Commission

interpretations.hypothesis: Registration of the EHIC with a Czech insurer is optional (European Commission: 'you can register').
Charles University says EU/EFTA students are 'obliged to register' with an auxiliary insurer after arrival.

items.title: Non-EU students: comprehensive private health insurance for the whole stay
items.title_it: Studenti extra-UE: assicurazione sanitaria privata completa per tutto il soggiorno
items.summary: Non-EU students without permanent residence are not in the public system unless employed, so for stays over 90 days they need comprehensive medical insurance meeting Act 326/1999 for the whole stay (or travel insurance for the first 90 days plus comprehensive after). Charles University has partner offers: PVZP (20% student discount, students under 35) and Slavia pojistovna (10% discount).
items.authority: Ministry of the Interior / Charles University
items.notes: CU lists exemptions for citizens of states with a health/social security treaty, Erasmus Mundus, Fulbright and UK GHIC holders. Under-18s need only travel insurance for the first 90 days (ipc.gov.cz).

items.title: Working for a Czech employer brings you into public health insurance
items.title_it: Lavorando per un datore ceco entri nell'assicurazione sanitaria pubblica

applies_to.min_work_hours: employment contract; on a DPP agreement only if monthly earnings reach CZK 12,000 (2026) with one employer

items.summary: Foreigners without permanent residence are insured in the public system as employees of an employer based in Czechia. A DPP agreement (dohoda o provedeni prace) counts as insured employment only in months when earnings with one employer reach CZK 12,000 (from 1 Jan 2026; previously above CZK 11,500). When a non-EU student's job ends, private comprehensive insurance is needed again.
items.notes: EU/EEA/Swiss workers are covered under EU regulations; EHIC is not used for the period of Czech insured employment. Earnings from DPP and DPC agreements are not added together.

items.title: Bank account: right to a basic payment account if legally resident
items.title_it: Conto bancario: diritto a un conto di base se legalmente residente

other: legally resident in an EU country

items.summary: Anyone legally resident in the EU is entitled to a basic payment account; banks cannot refuse it only because you do not live in the country. Charles University pays bursaries such as the accommodation bursary only to an account held at a bank in Czechia, so CU students who expect a bursary need a Czech account.
items.notes: No Czech authority page found listing documents banks require from foreign students; the EU right is general. Non-EU students: no official source found. CU notes that the EU registration certificate is commonly used as proof of a Czech address when opening an account (cuni.cz/UKEN-352.html).

items.title: Prague PID student season tickets (under 26), CU card as pass
items.title_it: Abbonamenti studenti PID a Praga (under 26), tessera UK come titolo

other: discount on season tickets only, not single tickets

items.summary: In Prague, full-time students up to their 26th birthday get discounted season tickets (not single tickets). Proof: school confirmation renewed each year or a valid ISIC; students studying abroad need a valid ISIC. Charles University student cards can be used as the PID pass or to load discounted tickets onto a Litacka card.
items.notes: Ages 15-18 get the discount regardless of student status; 10-15 and 65+ travel free in Prague with proof of age. Discount rules on the page are 'valid as of 1 April 2023'.

items.title: EU/EEA/Swiss students can work without any permit
items.title_it: Studenti UE/SEE/svizzeri possono lavorare senza permesso
items.summary: EU citizens (and Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, Switzerland) have free access to the labour market with the same rights as Czech citizens; no work permit, Employee Card or Blue Card is needed.

items.title: Non-EU full-time degree students: free access to the labour market
items.title_it: Studenti extra-UE iscritti a tempo pieno: libero accesso al lavoro

other: full-time study in an accredited university programme

items.summary: Third-country nationals studying full-time in an accredited university programme have free access to the labour market: no work permit needed and no statutory hour cap stated. Study must remain the main purpose of stay; Charles University recommends about 20 hours/week. Graduates of Czech universities keep free access permanently.

items.title: Non-EU exchange or distance students: only short work without a permit
items.title_it: Studenti extra-UE in scambio o a distanza: solo lavori brevi senza permesso
items.summary: According to Charles University, non-EU exchange students and distance-form students may work without an employment permit only up to age 26 and for at most 7 consecutive calendar days or 30 days in total per calendar year. Longer work requires a permit from the Labour Office unless another free-access ground applies (e.g. US, UK, Japan nationals).
items.notes: Rule taken from the university page; the ipc.gov.cz free-access page lists full-time students but does not state the 7/30-day exception, so not confirmed on a ministry page. ipc.gov.cz lists Australia, NZ, USA, Canada, UK, Israel, Japan, South Korea, Singapore, Taiwan as free-access nationalities.

items.title: Typical student job contract: DPP agreement, max 300 hours/year per employer
items.title_it: Contratto tipico per studenti: accordo DPP, max 300 ore/anno per datore
items.summary: The agreement to perform work (DPP) may cover at most 300 hours per calendar year with the same employer (hours of several DPPs with one employer are added). No social or health insurance is deducted in months when DPP earnings with one employer stay below CZK 12,000 (2026).
items.authority: Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs (MPSV) / VZP
items.notes: Hours with different employers are counted separately. Non-EU students still need free access to the labour market or a permit.

items.title: Statutory minimum wage
items.summary: From 1 January 2026 the minimum wage is CZK 22,400/month or CZK 134.40/hour (40-hour week). The government approved CZK 24,900/month and CZK 148.30/hour from 1 January 2027. No lower youth or student rate is mentioned on the MPSV pages.
items.authority: Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs (MPSV)
items.notes: 2027 press release dated 7 Sep 2026. Hourly rate is higher for shorter statutory weekly hours.
